outcomeInhibitoryEffect: A10 aptamer–labeled liposomes, the corresponding median lethal dose values are 3.70 × 10(1) (1.0 × 10−3), 1.85 × 10(3) (5.0 × 10−2), and 4.07 × 10(3) Bq/mL (1.1 × 10−1 μCi/mL), for LNCaP, Mat-Lu, and induced HUVEC, respectively.

name: A10
objectiveMechanism: DOX-loaded H40-PLA-PEG-Apt micelle for enhanced cellular uptake in PSMA-positive CWR22Rν1 cells, thereby enhancing cytotoxicity.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: IC50 of 1 μg/mL of DOX-loaded targeted unimolecular micelles with 76% tumor growth inhibition in vivo.

name: A10
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer–NCs bioconjugates to effectively target prostate-specific membrane antigen.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: 5.7 times more NCs were internalized into the cells than in the control.

name: A9 (CGA)7 extended aptamer
objectiveMechanism: Dox@Apt–hybr–TCL-SPION for enhanced Dox uptake and cytotoxicity.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Dox@Apt–hybr–TCL-SPIONs exerted a greater cytotoxic effect with cell viability of 42 ± 4% for targeted LNCaP versus 88 ± 6% for PC3; 53% tumor growth was inhibited in the Dox@Apt–hybr–TCL-SPION group than in the control.

name: A9 (CGA)7 extended aptamer
objectiveMechanism: Dox@Apt•dONT-DEN conjugate for targeted chemoimmunotherapy.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Enhanced Dox uptake with Dox@Apt•dONT-DEN (~ 94% for 22RV1 and 57% for LNCaP); 78% reduction in tumour volume in vivo.

name: Anti-EpCAM aptamer
objectiveMechanism: Ap-MSN-DOX nanoparticles for enhanced cellular uptake and increased cytotoxicity of the DOX.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Ap-MSN-DOX reduced the expression of EpCAM, while MSN-DOX caused no significant decrease and was more cytotoxic than MSN-DOX.

name: A10-3-J1
objectiveMechanism: SPIO-Apt-Dox NPs as a targeted drug delivery platform to PSMA+ prostate cancer cell.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Cell survival rate of LNCaP was only about 25.7% after being treated with doxorubicin-loaded A10-3-J1-SPIO-NPs.

name: A10-3.2
objectiveMechanism: MiRNA/ATE–APT delivery system to target PCa cells to reduce damage to the bone tissue and improve the therapeutic effect.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: MiRNA/ATE–APT had a 4.4-fold lower IC50 value (0.204 µM) than miRNA/ATE.

name: MUC1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: Apt conjugated hyaluronan/chitosan nanoparticles (HACSNPs) for targeted delivery of 5-FU to MUC1 overexpressing colorectal adenocarcinomas.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: IC50 value was significantly decreased to 1.43 ± 0.42 in HT-29 (MUC1+) cells with Apt-targeted nanoparticles than 3.63 ± 0.34 for Non-targeted nanoparticles.

name: MUC1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: pDNA/PEI/MUC1 aptamer complex for tumor-targeted gene delivery with high transfection efficiency.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Showed higher gene expressions than pDNA/PEI/non-specific aptamer complexes on the A549 cells.

name: MUC1 aptamer S2.2
objectiveMechanism: PTX-loaded Apt-NPs for enhanced drug delivery and cytotoxicity to MUC1+ cancer cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: PTX-Apt-NPs produced a more potent cytotoxicity than PTX-NPs or PTX-R-NPs in MCF-7 cells.

name: MUC1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: Doxo@Apt-DNA-icosa for specific internalization to kill epithelial cancer cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Doxo@Apt-DNA-icosa showed a greater cytotoxicity than free doxorubicin and Doxo@DNA-icosa.

name: MUC1-(CGA)7 extended aptamer
objectiveMechanism: DNR–MUC1–QDs probe for imaging and sensing the delivery of DNR to targeted prostate tumour cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: LOD = for DNR was 19 nmol/L with a linear concentration range of 33–88 nmol/L.
cytotoxicityCellViability: MUC1–QDs conjugates had no obvious effect on the cell viability of PC-3M cells at concentrations up to 0.112 nmol/L.

name: MA3
objectiveMechanism: Apt-Dox for specific drug delivery to MUC1-positive cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: MA3 treatment generated fluorescence signals that were significantly more potent than random DNA treatment in MCF7 cells.

name: MA3
objectiveMechanism: Apt-Dox for specific drug delivery to MUC1-positive cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Selectively deliver the cytotoxic agent doxorubicin to MUC1-positive cells, while reducing the drug uptake by MUC1-negative cells.

name: Modified MUC1 aptamer S2.2
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-CdTe QDs for active tumor-targeted imaging in vitro and in vivo.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Tumor organs showed higher accumulation of the targeting aptamer-QDs.

name: MA3
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-modified Iron nanoparticles for enhanced targeted hyperthermia damage to MUC1-positive cancer cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Apt-NPs significantly enhanced the hyperthermia damage to MCF-7 cells (p < 005), but not that to HepG2 cells.

name: MUC1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: MUC1 aptamer-functionalized hybrid nanoparticles to selectively deliver miRNA-29b to MUC1-expressing cancer cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: MUC1 aptamer miRNA-29b-loaded hybrid nanoparticles effectively downregulate DNMT3b and MCL, leading to superior induction of apoptosis and also display superior antiproliferative effects.

name: MUC-1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-Au@SPIONs for MR imaging and photothermal therapy.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Cytotoxicity was 94%, 90%, and 79% after 2, 4, and 8 minutes of irradiation, respectively, at 100 μg/ml of aptamer-Au@SPIONs.

name: MUC-1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: MUC1-AgNCm-miR-34a for targeted delivery and inhibiting oncogene expression and inducing apoptosis in carcinomas.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Efficiently enhance the intracellular delivery of miR-34a and show higher down-regulation of BCL-2 and CCND1 protein expression levels.

name: MUC-1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: DOX–KLA–anti-MUC1–micelle for the targeted co-delivery and antitumor effects.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: The IC50 of DOX–KLA–anti-MUC1–micelle was 1 μM, resulting in a 28.3% level of apoptosis and necrosis.
stability: Size of KLA–anti-MUC1–micelle remained intact until 6 hours of incubation in either PBS or FBS 50% at 37°C.

name: 5TR1
objectiveMechanism: Epi-PLGA-CS-Apt for targeted therapy of tumor cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: MCF7 cells viability after treatment with Epi-PLGA-CS, Epi and Epi-PLGA-CS-Apt were 33.84% ± 3.5, 35.50% ± 2.4, and 34.22% ± 2.80, respectively.
cytotoxicityCellViability: CHO cells viability after treatment with Epi-PLGA-CS-Apt was 92.4% ± 5.9.

name: MUC1 aptamer
objectiveMechanism: APT-DOX-loaded hydrogels to promote the uptake of DOX into the cell.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: The average relative tumour volume of APT-DOX-CS/GP was significantly reduced to 107.41% on the sixth day.

name: Sgc8-linker
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-based DNA dendrimer for targeted therapeutic effect of Dox.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Dox-G3-sgc8 showed a similar inhibition of cell proliferation as free Dox.

name: Sgc8
objectiveMechanism: Poly-Aptamer-Drug for enhanced targeting and killing leukemia cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Poly-Aptamer-Drug (10 nm) for 24 h resulted in a ~50% loss of viability of CCRF-CEM cells, significantly higher than that of Dox alone or Mono-Aptamer-Drug.

name: HB5
objectiveMechanism: Identify an aptamer targeting HER2 and develop an apt-Dox conjugate for in vitro targeting and delivery of Dox to breast cancer cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Selectively deliver Dox to HER2-positive breast cancer cells.
kdValue: 18.9 nM (for HER2 peptide) and 316 nM (for ER2 ECD protein)

name: Sgc8c
objectiveMechanism: Dau-aptamer-SWNTs to enhance targeted delivery of Dau to target Molt-4 cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Molt-4 cell viability after treatment with Dau-aptamer-SWNTs tertiary complex was 38.1 ± 5.4%.
cytotoxicityCellViability: U266 cell viability after treatment with Dau-aptamer-SWNTs was 78.9 ± 7.2%.

name: Sgc8
objectiveMechanism: DOX-SMN for specific binding and uptake to the target cancer cells.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: A smaller IC50 of 0.27 μM was obtained for DOX-SMNs than for DOX only (0.39 μM).

name: Sgc8
objectiveMechanism: MSN-Dox@EGCg-Apt to improve tumor targeting and cellular uptake.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: MSN-Dox@EGCg-Apt exhibited slightly higher inhibition of cell proliferation than free Dox and targeted the in vivo tumour via receptor-mediated endocytosis in the CEM cells.

name: Sgc8c
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-modified capsids ( MS2-1-A ) for a photodynamic treatment.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Selectively kill more than 76% of the Jurkat cells after only 20 min of illumination.

name: Sgc8c
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-conjugated/DOX-loaded (ADD) droplets for targeting, imaging and therapy.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: 56.8% decrease in cell viability with aptamer-conjugated droplets, representing a 4.5-fold increase in comparison to non-conjugated droplets.

name: HB5
objectiveMechanism: MSCN-PEG-HB5/DOX nanoparticle for chemo-photothermal combined tumor-targeted therapy.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Showed much higher DOX accumulation at the tumor site than MSCN-PEG/DOX and showed a significant decrease of IC50 in combined therapy with DOX 6.71 μg/ml.
cytotoxicityCellViability: Hemolytic percentage of MSCN-based nanoparticles was less than 5% even at the highest concentration (500 μg/ml).

name: S6
objectiveMechanism: Isolate RNA aptamers that specifically bind to a HER-2-overexpressing human breast cancer cell line.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: N/A

name: TSA14
objectiveMechanism: Aptamer-PL-Dox to improve cellular uptake and cytotoxicity of PL-Dox in TUBO breast cell line.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: 4.5-fold (IC50 = 12.54 ± 4.38 μmol ) more cytotoxic than Doxil-mimic, with a final mean tumour volume of 145.8 ± 33.047 mm³ in vivo.

name: Anti-CD44 thioaptamer
objectiveMechanism: TA-NPs for targeted microRNA-145 (miR-145) deliver.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: IC50 value of MDA-MB-231 was 0.118 µM, approximately 1.14-fold lower IC50 value than PEG-PAMAM/miRNA; Mean tumour weight of TA-PEG-PAMAM/miRNA groups was 0.41 g in vivo.

name: EpCAM Apt

outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Apt-CUR-NP was significantly more potent against HT29 cells compared to HEK293T cells (cell viabilities of 58.9% ± 2.6% and 72.4% ± 1.3%, respectively; P < 0.05). In vivo, a sixfold increase of t1/2 compared to free CUR.

name: GBI-10

outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Enhanced (~2.01-fold) cellular binding of GTLs than NTLs, with a T1 value of GTLs (593.4 ms ±5.9 ms), was significantly lower (P<0.01) than the other group in C6 cells.

name: GBI-10
objectiveMechanism: QD–Apt nanoprobe as a diagnostic for recognize tenascin-C on the human glioma cell surface.
outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Specifically and exactly recognize tenascin-C on the U251 cell membrane.

outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Cell viability of MDA-MB-231 at 24 h after ultrasound irradiation with DOX-loaded APT/TSP liposomes was 60%.

outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Doxorubicin was markedly increased, compared to the free doxorubicin and DOTAP: DOPE/DOX group.

outcomeInhibitoryEffect: Reduced cell viability up to 60–70% compared to the untreated cells or control conjugate upon Gint4.T-STAT3 treatment; AsiC reduced cell migration by approximately 60–65%.

stability: Gint4.T-STAT3 complex is highly stable in human serum, remaining undigested up to 24 h in 85% serum.

outcomeInhibitoryEffect: HEH can reduce cell viability by 90% in SKBR3 cells and 85% in BT474 cells; Apoptotic and necrotic cells increased by 18.72% after 48 h and 39.63% after 72 h and 5–6-fold reduction in tumor sizes compared with the PBS-treated tumors.

name: HER2 aptamer

name: MUC1 aptamer

name: AS1411

name: AS1411
objectiveMechanism: Electrochemiluminescence based on aptamer modified bipolar electrode mounted into 3D printed microchannel for detection of human breast cancer cells.

name: MUC1 aptamer

name: AS1411
